bodyHtml:
NDT training and certification program in the USA: how it works

In the USA, an NDT training and certification program is run by the employer. The employer adopts ASNT SNT-TC-1A through its own written practice. Technicians complete classroom training, log on-the-job experience and pass general, specific and practical examinations set under a Level III. Then the employer certifies them. A training provider supplies the training hours. It does not issue the certification. The certificate belongs to the employer's program.

This section is for the people who run that program: operations managers, QA/QC leads and training managers. It covers how to set the program up, what a training plan should contain, how to handle experienced hires, nationwide contracts and aerospace work, and the mistakes that show up at audit. For course dates and costs, see the US course list and published fees. To get a plan for your own crew, request a training plan.

Setting up an employer NDT program, stage by stage

Most companies that ask for "NDT training" actually need a program, not a course. The course is one stage. The order of the stages matters, because each one produces evidence the next one depends on.

StageWhat happensWho owns itWhat sets the pace
1. ScopeList every method and technique you sell or use, and the level each person needsEmployerYour contracts and client specs
2. Written practiceAdopt SNT-TC-1A, or CP-189 if a client requires it, as your own controlled documentEmployer, approved by its Level IIINumber of methods and client requirements
3. TrainingClassroom and practical hours per method and level, as the written practice setsTraining provider, in-house or contractedScheduling around shifts and jobs
4. ExperienceOn-the-job hours per method, logged and signedEmployer and its Level IIsReal work. This stage cannot be compressed
5. ExaminationsGeneral, specific and practical, graded and filedLevel III, in-house or outsourcedCandidates' readiness and examiner availability
6. CertificationEmployer issues the certificate for method and levelEmployerComplete files for each person
7. MaintenanceVision checks, recertification, new methods, written practice revisionsEmployer and Level IIIDue dates in the written practice

Two points catch new programs out. First, stage 2 comes before stage 3. Training delivered before the written practice exists may not match the hours and content the document later sets. Second, stage 4 sets the calendar. You can run classroom training in a week. You cannot collect months of supervised UT experience in a week. Plan the start dates of your trainees around when you need them certified, not around when the course runs.

If you do not have a Level III to approve the written practice and run the examinations, that is a consulting job rather than a training one. See ASNT Level III consulting services.

What a training plan from Atlantis contains

A training plan turns your written practice into a schedule for named people. It is the document we send back when you request one, and it is built from your crew list, not from our course catalog.

Part of the planWhat it containsWhy it matters at audit
Crew matrixEach person, the methods and levels they need, and what evidence they already holdShows the program covers every method you put your name to
Gap listHours still owed per person, per method, against your written practiceStops anyone being certified on hours they never completed
Delivery scheduleLive online theory sessions and onsite practical blocks, set around your shiftsKeeps crews on the tools while training is completed
Practical contentExercises on specimens and geometries that match your actual workPractical examinations are easier to defend when training matched the work
Training recordsAttendance, hours, topics and dates per person, per method and levelThe first thing an auditor samples in a certification file
Examination planWhich examinations follow, and who administers them under your written practiceSeparates training from examination, as SNT-TC-1A expects
Maintenance calendarVision check and recertification dates for everyone on the matrixLapsed vision and expired certificates are the easiest findings to avoid

We deliver Level I, II and III training to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, live online or onsite at your facility. There is no physical training centre. Practical blocks run on your equipment wherever possible, because that is the equipment your technicians will be examined and certified on. Between sessions, trainees can practise setups on Practical NDT, our 3D skills simulator. It supports practice. It does not replace hands-on hours or the practical examination.

Hiring a technician certified somewhere else

Under SNT-TC-1A, a certificate from a previous employer belongs to that employer's program. Your company is not obliged to accept it. But you do not have to start the person from zero either. The written practice should state how prior training and experience are credited. In practice, a careful employer does this:

  1. Get the records, not just the card. Ask for the training hours with dates and source, the experience log and the examination grades from the previous employer.
  2. Verify them. Contact the previous employer or its Level III. Records that cannot be verified should not be credited.
  3. Credit what matches. Training and experience that meet your written practice for the same method and level can be credited. Hours for a different technique, such as conventional UT counted toward PAUT, should not be.
  4. Examine on your work. Most employers at least set their own specific and practical examinations, because those test your procedures and your equipment.
  5. Check vision. Run a vision examination at hire, whatever the old file says.
  6. Certify and file. Issue your own certificate, and keep the evidence for each credited item in the file.

This is often the fastest route to adding certified people. It is also where weak programs get caught, because a credited hour with no record behind it is still an uncredited hour to an auditor.

Nationwide contracts and multi-state crews

There is no state NDT licence for UT, MT, PT, VT or ET technicians. An SNT-TC-1A certification issued by your company is valid wherever your company works, because it is your program. That is why one written practice can cover crews in Texas, Louisiana, California and anywhere else. What changes on a nationwide contract is the client's checking, not the certificate.

  • One written practice, applied the same way everywhere. Crews at different sites should be trained, examined and filed to the same document. Different branches running their own versions is a common finding on multi-site audits.
  • Client acceptance. National operators and EPCs often review your written practice and a sample of files before approving you for all their sites. Some specify CP-189 instead of SNT-TC-1A. Check the contract before you mobilise.
  • Subcontracted crews. If a subcontractor supplies technicians, they work under the subcontractor's certification, not yours. The prime contractor should check those records before they arrive on site.
  • Radiography is different. Industrial radiographers also need radiation safety certification under NRC rules or the rules of the Agreement State where they work. That layer is separate from SNT-TC-1A and has to be checked state by state.
  • Records available from anywhere. A client at a site in one state should be able to see a technician's current certification without waiting for a file from head office.

For more on how national clients check certifications, read NDT certification on nationwide US contracts. Our state hubs cover local delivery and industries: Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, California and Pennsylvania.

Crews crossing into Canada. Canada mostly certifies NDT personnel as individuals, not through employer programs. The CGSB closed on 1 April 2026. Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body continues and issues certification to CAN/CGSB-48.9712. A US crew sent to a Canadian site may need that certification, depending on the owner and the jurisdiction. See NDT training in Canada.

Aerospace work and NAS 410: where SNT-TC-1A training stops

Searches for aerospace NDT courses and NAS 410 training usually come from people who expect one course to cover both. It does not. US aerospace suppliers qualify NDT personnel to NAS 410, set by the aerospace industry and enforced by the primes and through Nadcap audits. Like SNT-TC-1A it is employer-based, but its requirements are mandatory rather than recommended, and it has its own rules for the Responsible Level 3, training hours and examinations.

Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. We do not offer NAS 410 training or certification. If you work in aerospace:

  • Ask your Responsible Level 3 or your prime what training they accept toward NAS 410 before you book anything.
  • Do not assume SNT-TC-1A hours will be credited. That decision belongs to your aerospace employer's program.
  • If your company does both industrial and aerospace work, keep two clearly separate certification tracks. Mixing them in one written practice causes findings on both sides.

Many companies in California, Washington and the Gulf Coast do industrial work under SNT-TC-1A alongside aerospace work. For the industrial side, a training plan works as described on this page.

If you are looking for NDT certification as an individual

Many searches for "NDT certification near me" or "NDT classes" come from people without an employer yet. Here is how it works in the US.

  • Classroom training you can do now. You can complete classroom hours for Level I and Level II before you are hired. With us that is live online, so location does not matter. Keep the attendance records. A future employer will want them.
  • Experience and certification come with a job. Under SNT-TC-1A, you log experience hours and take the employer's examinations once you are working. The employer then certifies you. No school can do this part for you.
  • Third-party routes exist. ASNT's central certification programs and ISO 9712 certification bodies issue certificates to individuals. They are useful, but many US employers still certify you under their own written practice as well.
  • Level III candidates. If you are aiming for Level III, the usual route is ASNT's Level III examinations, then certification by your employer. We run Level III training led by an ASNT Level III. Our founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, is one.

Atlantis has trained 1,000+ technicians, most of them sent by their employers. If you are an employer building a crew, request a training plan and send your crew list.

How to compare NDT training providers

Training managers usually compare providers on dates and cost. Both matter, but neither tells you whether the hours will stand up when an auditor opens a certification file. These questions do.

Question to askA good answerA warning sign
Which scheme do you train to?A clear answer, for example SNT-TC-1A only, with the levels and methods listed"All schemes", or a promise that one course covers SNT-TC-1A, NAS 410 and ISO 9712
Will the course match our written practice?They ask to see it, then map hours and topics to itThey never ask what your written practice says
What records do we get?Attendance, actual instruction hours, topics and dates per person, method and levelA single completion certificate per person
Who teaches?A named instructor whose method qualifications you can check"Our certified team"
How is the practical done?On your equipment or specimens that match your workA generic demonstration nobody touches
Do you issue certification?No. The employer certifies under its written practice"Certified in five days", or a wallet card issued by the school
Can you work around our shifts?Split cohorts, theory online, practical blocks onsiteOne fixed public date, take it or leave it

The answer to "do you issue certification?" is the most useful filter. Under SNT-TC-1A, a provider who says yes is either running a third-party scheme, which is a different thing, or is telling you something your auditor will not accept.

Ask for a sample training record before you book. If it would not survive a client's file review, the course will not either, however good the teaching is. And check who will hold the records afterwards. They belong in your files, not only on the provider's system.

Common mistakes employers make with NDT training

  • Buying a course before writing the program. The training then has to be checked against a written practice written afterwards. Sometimes it does not fit.
  • Treating a course certificate as certification. A course certificate proves training hours. The employer certifies, after experience and examinations.
  • Letting the trainer also be the only examiner, with no separation. SNT-TC-1A expects examinations controlled by a Level III. Keep training records and examination records separate in the file.
  • Generic practicals. A crew that inspects pipe welds should practise on pipe welds. Flat plates prove little.
  • Counting hours by the calendar. A week-long course is not 40 hours of training if half of it was paperwork and breaks. Log actual instruction time.
  • Missing the maintenance stage. Vision checks and recertification lapse quietly. Put the dates in a system that warns you in advance.
  • Training on equipment the crew will never use. Practical skill transfers best on the instruments and probes in your own cabinet.

Frequently asked questions

What is an NDT program?

An NDT program is the employer's system for training, examining, certifying and recertifying its NDT personnel. In the US it is usually built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and written down in the employer's written practice, which a Level III approves.

Is there ASNT training near me?

Atlantis has no physical training centre. Theory runs live online, so it is available anywhere in the US, and practical blocks run onsite at the employer's facility. Our state pages explain local delivery.

Is SNT-TC-1A training the same as SNT-TC-1A certification?

No. Training supplies the classroom and practical hours. Certification is issued by the employer after experience hours and examinations under its written practice.

Do you offer NAS 410 or aerospace NDT certification training?

No. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Aerospace suppliers qualify personnel to NAS 410, and your Responsible Level 3 decides what training it accepts.

Does ASNT certification work on nationwide contracts?

An employer's SNT-TC-1A certification is valid wherever that employer works, since there is no state licence for most NDT methods. National clients still review your written practice and technician files, and radiography adds state or NRC radiation safety requirements.

Can I get NDT certification online?

You can complete classroom training online. Certification under SNT-TC-1A also needs logged experience and examinations, including a hands-on practical, and is issued by your employer.

How long does it take to certify a new technician?

Classroom training takes days or weeks. Experience hours take longer and set the timeline, so the total is usually measured in months for Level II. Your written practice sets the minimums.

Can you deliver training onsite at our plant or shop?

Yes. Onsite delivery at the employer is one of our two delivery modes, the other being live online. Most employers combine them: theory online around the shift pattern, practical blocks onsite on their own equipment and specimens.

Do you train candidates for ASNT Level III?

Yes. Level III training is led by an ASNT NDT Level III. ASNT runs the Level III examinations themselves, and your employer then certifies you as its Level III under its written practice.

Where can I see course dates and fees?

The US course list and published fees page lists courses by method and level. This page covers how the employer-based program around those courses works. The training hub lists all programs.
